team|Team]]}} }} '''Kevin Wesley Love''' (born September 7, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is a five-time [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] and a two-time member of the [[All-NBA Second Team]], winning an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in [[2016 NBA Finals|2016]]. He was also a member of the gold medal-winning [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] and the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]]. In 2011, Love won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] and led the league in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]]. The son of former NBA player [[Stan Love (basketball)|Stan Love]], Love was a top-ranked prospect out of [[Lake Oswego High School]] in Oregon. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] and led the team to a [[Final four|Final Four]] appearance in the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008 NCAA tournament]]. Love was named a consensus [[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|First Team All-American]] and was voted [[Pac-10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|player of the year]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-10 Conference]] (now Pac-12). He elected to forgo his remaining three years of college eligibility and entered the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He was taken fifth overall by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], and was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on draft night for the third overall selection, [[O. J. Mayo]], in an eight-player deal. During the 2010–11 season, Love established the longest streak for consecutive games recording [[double-double|double figures in points and rebounds]] since the [[ABA–NBA merger]]. After six seasons with Minnesota, Love was traded to the Cavaliers in 2014. After making four straight [[NBA Finals]] with the team and winning a championship, Love suffered multiple injuries from 2018 to 2021. He slotted into a reserve role in 2021–22 and finished as runner-up for the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award|Sixth Man of the Year]] award. However, reduced playing time the following season led Love to reach a contract buyout agreement with the Cavaliers. Love helped the Bruins to the Final Four of the tournament, where they lost to the [[2007–08 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis Tigers]], whose season and tournament appearance, in turn, were later vacated. At the end of the 2007–08 regular season, Love was named [[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus first-team All-American]], [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]], [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]], and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]]. 52591001920.jpg|thumb|Love in 2022]] In [[2021–22 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2021–22]], Love became a reserve for the first time since early in his career.{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Mannix|title=Kevin Love Is Having Fun in Cleveland Again|date=April 5, 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/04/05/kevin-love-cavaliers-lebron-james-future|access-date=April 26, 2022}} Against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on December 31, 2021, he had 35 points on 10-for-18 shooting, including a 7-for-14 on 3-pointers, for his highest-scoring game in over four seasons.{{cite news|first=Kane|last=Pitman|title=Kevin Love's resurgence continues as Sixth Man of the Year case builds|date=January 1, 2022|work=Sporting News|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/kevin-love-cleveland-cavaliers-sixthman/czeo8zae9n611f5idr3ck6wev|access-date=April 26, 2022}} He was the runner-up for the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] after averaging 13.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists.{{cite news|first=Camryn|last=Justice|title=Cavs' Evan Mobley, Darius Garland, Kevin Love named finalists for 2021-22 NBA Awards|date=April 17, 2022|website=News5Cleveland.com|url=https://www.news5cleveland.com/sports/basketball/cavaliers/cavs-evan-mobley-darius-garland-kevin-love-named-finalists-for-2021-22-nba-awards|access-date=April 26, 2022}}{{Cite press release|title=Heat's Tyler Herro wins 2021-22 Kia Sixth Man of the Year award |date=May 3, 2022|publisher=NBA|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-22-kia-sixth-man-of-the-year |access-date=May 3, 2022 |language=en}} On February 18, 2023, Love and the Cavaliers officially agreed to a contract buyout, making him a free agent. However, the Heat went on to lose the Finals in 5 games to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|first=Shaun|last=Powell|title=5 takeaways: Nuggets drop Heat for 1st NBA championship|url=https://www.nba.com/news/5-takeaways-nuggets-win-title-game-5|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2023|access-date=June 13, 2023}} On July 6, 2023, Love re-signed with the Heat on a two-year, $7.9 million contract, with a player option for the second year.{{cite web|title=HEAT Re-sign Kevin Love|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-sign-kevin-love|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} He made 55 appearances (five starts) for Miami during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 8.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.
